title: Domain and state ownership audit for the F-GC45 real-SWAP/MODFLOW fixture

swap_fixture_domain.native_length_unit: centimetre for the lower-face hydraulic construction, because dz/2 is passed as bottom_half_distance_cm
swap_fixture_domain.initial_pressure_head_profile_rule: heads(1)=-75 cm; each next node adds node_distance=1 native cm

coupled_head_semantics.predictor: SWAP bottom-face pressure head is converted to hydraulic interface head H=z_face+psi.
coupled_head_semantics.canonical_source_statement: The prescribed-qbot bottom-face module states: 'This is the coupling-plane head. It is not the freatic groundwater level.'
coupled_head_semantics.corrector: MODFLOW/interface hydraulic head is converted back to SWAP bottom pressure head and assigned to bottom_head under bottom mode 5.
coupled_head_semantics.internal_groundwater_level_mutation: No source-level evidence that the head forcing adapter overwrites the SWAP physical state's groundwater_level field; it materializes bottom_head forcing only.
coupled_head_semantics.classification: SHARED_INTERFACE_HEAD / DIRICHLET_BOUNDARY_STATE, not established as SHARED_PHREATIC_WATER_TABLE_STATE

ownership_findings: The F-GC45 MODFLOW STO volume and the F-GC45 SWAP/FMR column are not declared or constructed as the same geometrically coextensive physical storage volume.
The synthetic MODFLOW cell is 2 m thick with Sy/Ss storage, whereas the SWAP test column uses the legacy four-node centimetre-scale fixture geometry.
Therefore coexistence of MODFLOW STO and a nonzero finite-window SWAP response u in F-GC45 does not by itself demonstrate duplicate physical storage.
MAP10's u approximately J_S relation characterizes the SWAP column's finite-window response to its bottom-interface head; it does not establish identity with the MODFLOW cell's Sy.
The current real-SWAP fixture is closer to a head-matched boundary coupling than to the Van Walsum/Veldhuizen complete-profile phreatic shared-state h-link.
implications_for_dummy_testbank: DSW02 remains a valid proof of what duplicate storage would look like if two components represent the same physical storage volume.
DSW08 remains the valid two-state finite-resistance comparison.
A new transparent coextensive-domain test is required to map the shared-phreatic h-link concept onto MODFLOW STO; F-GC45 cannot serve as that proof.
vocabulary_correction: Use 'shared interface hydraulic head' for current F-GC production unless a specific fixture proves that the interface head is the phreatic water-table state.
Reserve 'shared phreatic state' for models where both components explicitly represent the same water-table state and combined profile storage ownership is defined.
forbidden_inference: Do not claim F-GC45 has double-counted storage from u and Sy alone.
Do not claim F-GC45 implements the SIMGRO/MetaSWAP h-link complete-profile storage contract.
Do not infer a physical finite-resistance q-link merely because the coupling occurs at a lower boundary.
No production source change follows from this audit.
next: Update research taxonomy/primer to distinguish shared interface head from shared phreatic state.
Design a coextensive-domain manufactured SWAP/MODFLOW ownership experiment if production architecture is intended to support a true phreatic shared-state h-link.
Keep MAP08/MAP09 as independent corrector-domain/process-response investigations.
